resources.string: How to Play Nine Men\'s Morris

Each player has nine men (six in the short game). Take turns placing one man on any empty point.

Three of your men in a row on a line make a mill, and a mill lets you remove one opponent man from the board. Men in a mill are protected unless every opponent man is in a mill.

Once all men are placed, slide one man per turn to a neighbouring empty point. With flying on, a player down to three men may jump to any empty point.

You win when your opponent has only two men left or cannot move. If nobody makes a mill for a long time, it is a draw.

How to Play Hare and Hounds

Three hounds chase one hare on an 11-point board. The hounds move first.

Hounds can only step forward (to the right) or straight up and down along a line, never back. The hare can step to any neighbouring empty point.

The hounds win by trapping the hare so it cannot move. The hare wins by slipping past all three hounds, by leaving the hounds with no move, or by surviving 20 hound moves.
